title: AUTOMATIC SPRINKLER SYSTEM
officialText:
1506.1 Sprinkler systems during alteration or demolition. Existing sprinkler systems in
buildings undergoing an alteration or demolition shall comply with the requirements of Section
3303.7.4 of the New York City Building Code and Section 1506.2.
1506.2 Sprinkler protection during construction in fully sprinklered buildings. Where
alterations are proposed to a floor on which the sprinkler system is to be temporarily disconnected
in the work area, Temporary Core Sprinkler Protection (TCSP) shall be provided in accordance
with Sections 1506.2.1 through 1506.2.5. Alterations shall also comply with the New York City
Fire Code, including referenced standards therein.
1506.2.1 Temporary Core Sprinkler Protection (TCSP). As a temporary fire protection
measure, TCSP shall be provided on occupied floors on which an existing sprinkler system is
to be temporarily disconnected during alterations. When provided, TCSP shall be connected
to the fire alarm system in the building. In buildings without a fire alarm system, TCSP shall
be connected to a local annunciation and notification system. TCSP shall comply with and
shall be placed in accordance with applicable requirements of NFPA 13 as modified by
Appendix Q of the New York City Building Code. TCSP shall provide the same responses as
the existing sprinkler system monitoring in the building. TCSP shall be provided at the
following locations:
1. At the elevator hoistway openings.
2. At exit doors to required exit stairways.
3. Along the egress paths, including corridors, connecting all required exits and elevator
lobbies.
1506.2.2 Sprinkler protection on partially occupied floors. When a floor is partially
occupied during an alteration, the sprinkler heads in the work area may be temporarily removed
and the TCSP that complies with Section 1506.2.1 shall not be required provided all the
following conditions are met:
1. The work area does not exceed 52,000 square feet (4831 m2) and is fully compartmented
in at least 1- hour fire-rated barriers or horizontal assemblies;
2. The entire floor’s sprinkler system remains intact outside of the work area;
3. Sprinkler head(s) are placed on both sides of all entrances to and exits from the work
area;
Exceptions:
1. Spaces located outside of the first floor entrances and exits.
2. Openings to exit enclosures.
4. Heat detectors are placed on the construction side of the entrance doors to the temporary
compartmented work area. Heat detectors shall be installed in compliance with NFPA 72
as modified by Appendix Q of the New York City Building Code for the occupancy in
which they are placed and shall be connected to the fire alarm system in the building.
Where there is no fire alarm system, heat detectors shall be connected to a local
annunciation and notification system;
5. Sprinkler heads are not placed inside the stairwell when the work area is near the
stairwell;
6. All required exits are maintained for the duration of the construction, including those
from the work area; and
7. Application for a permanent replacement sprinkler system is made within 60 days of
application filed for the temporary removal of sprinklers.
1506.2.3 Sprinkler protection on unoccupied floors. TCSP, as described in Section
1506.2.1, shall be provided when an entire floor is unoccupied during an alteration in a fully
sprinklered existing building. The sprinklers shall be located at an appropriate height above
the floor to clear any future ductwork and sprinklers and shall comply with and be placed in
accordance with Section 903 of the New York City Building Code.
1506.2.4 Scope of work with duration of 1 year or more. Where the alteration work is
expected to take a year or longer, temporary protection measures described in Sections
1506.2.2 and 1506.2.3 shall not be permitted and the entire floor(s) undergoing alterations shall
be sprinklered in accordance with Section 903 of the New York City Building Code.
1506.2.5 Compliance with the New York City Fire Code. Where temporary removal or
disconnection of sprinkler system is permitted in accordance with Sections 1506.2.2 or
1506.2.3, the building owner shall comply with the New York City Fire Code out-of-service
requirements.
